transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The Trump administration is lowering fuel efficiency standards that new cars and light
trucks are required to meet in five years.
Biden-era rules that centered around climate action put the threshold at a combined fleet-wide
average of 50.4 miles per gallon.
President Trump is lowering it to 34.9 because he says it's good for the seller, the buyer,
and the overall economy.
Here's NPR's Willa Rubin.
The corporate average fuel economy, CAFE standards, have been around since the '70s.
These require American carmakers to make each year's new vehicles more fuel efficient on
average across their entire fleets.
But how much more efficient?
Under the Biden administration, fleets needed to get 2% more efficient every year.
Comment, carmakers needed to make electric vehicles balance out their gas guzzlers, otherwise
they were subject to a fine.
That fine went away last July as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Now, a much smaller increase in fuel efficiency will be required every year.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
The U.S. Senate is in session for one more week before lawmakers head to the campaign
trails for the midterm elections.
Many are feuding with the Trump White House over its unilateral decision to cancel more
than $800 million in funding Congress had already approved.
NPR's Eric McDaniel explains what's at stake.
Of the $810 million being withheld, $567 million comes from programs that provided services
to refugees, asylees, and other non-citizens, according to a memo from the White House.
Obviously, a group that has received a brunt of negative attention from the president.
I just want to be crystal clear here.
This pocket rescission that we're talking about is illegal.
NPR's Eric McDaniel reporting.
Five British nationals described as "terror suspects" have now been released on bail.
They were detained Sunday near a British military base used by the United States to launch strikes
on Iran.
That location prompted concerns about a connection to the Middle East.
NPR's Lauren Frayer has the latest from London.
British counterterrorism officials say the men are still under investigation for explosives
and terrorism offenses, and that authorities are investigating multiple lines of inquiry,
including whether the suspects were working for Iran, Russia, or other non-state groups
"knowingly or unknowingly."
Iran's embassy in London denies any involvement, saying malicious speculation only fuels Iranophobia.
The men, Londoners all in their mid-20s, were detained in the middle of the night near RAF
Royal Air Force Base, Fairford, west of London.
It's been the target of anti-war protesters as well.
Lauren Frayer, NPR News, London.
This is NPR News.
More than a year after floods killed 27 campers and counselors at Camp Mystic in Texas, the
Riverfront Properties owners are looking to sell.
The Christian Girls Camp filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection a few days ago.
The Eastland family sought to reopen the camp this summer, but the families of those who
died in the 2025 floods strongly oppose that as investigations into the tragedy continue.
After just over a year on the job, FBI Deputy Director Andrew Bailey says he's resigning.
He is one of two deputy directors at the Bureau.
Smart Universities are rolling out courses to help people cope with concerns about artificial
intelligence and adapt to the technology.
And Piers Windsor-Johnson reports a new course on AI gets underway this week at Harvard University.
Some people are rushing to try every new AI tool.
Others say they want nothing to do with it.
Experts say both reactions can be driven by anxiety.
Harvard Medical School psychologist Luana Marquez helped develop a new course to address
those fears.
I think there's a level of fear of the unknown that makes sense, but we need to be able to
train people to adjust.
And so that is why we created the course, because we have a pressure cooker that's getting louder
and louder.
Ohio State is also adding AI skills across its undergraduate curriculum.
Miami University in Ohio offers a self-paced AI fundamentals course for students, faculty,
and staff.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump administration lowers fuel efficiency standards for new cars and light trucks to 34.9 mpg
Senate feuds with Trump White House over cancellation of $810 million in congressionally approved funding
Five British nationals described as terror suspects released on bail near RAF Fairford military base
Camp Mystic in Texas files for bankruptcy over year after floods killed 27 people
FBI Deputy Director Andrew Bailey resigns after just over one year in position
Universities including Harvard roll out courses to help people cope with artificial intelligence anxiety
